coverage.extractionControl: PDF text extraction duplicates some coloured/bold Greek letters in Table66. The rendered page was inspected; repeated extraction characters are not counted as source innovations. Full Greek/Hebrew diplomatic re-edition is not claimed.

inspectedMethod.result: Subgrouping distinguishes derived shared innovations from shared retentions. Matching features also require consideration of independent development and diffusion.
inspectedMethod.condition: The direction of change and comparison domain must be justified; similarity alone does not determine genealogy.

inspectedMethod.result: Genealogy and contact remain separate parts of the account. Vernacular susceptibility can help distinguish reading traditions, but Kantor also asks for innovations supporting genetic relations.
inspectedMethod.condition: Do not replace one arbitrary ancestry tree with an undifferentiated similarity network.

inspectedMethod.result: The proposed proto-reading background allows internal diversity; some community reading differences can arise from applying a vernacular dialect to a text.
inspectedMethod.condition: A uniform ancestral recital or a parent reading tradition for every branch is not automatically established.

inspectedMethod.result: Notation may imitate a prestigious tradition. Same-reading manuscript comparisons can expose normalization, including scribal alteration distinct from living recitation change.
inspectedMethod.condition: Script, copying layer, vocalization system and spoken realization remain distinct evidence levels.

concreteCharacters.sourceClaimStatus: Author's proposed innovation and supporting argument inspected; underlying manuscript and external chronology claims not independently reproduced
concreteCharacters.feature: Rounding/raising of historically long a into the rounded qameṣ vowel
concreteCharacters.qualification: These are contextual examples of a reconstructed feature, not the same lexical token across all traditions. The author discusses ambiguous transcription and change chronology before proposing a shared innovation.
missingIndependentPremises: Original witness collation behind cited editions
concreteCharacters.sunnyUse: A feature record can carry the proposed change, its environment, date constraints, counterexamples and uncertainty. The written vowel does not prescribe an acoustic frequency or musical pitch.

concreteCharacters.sunnyUse: The feature's grammatical function and environment matter; a global letter-name match cannot replace them.

proposedSunnyReuse.status: Source-informed investigative criterion, selected by actual Jev; no central ontology or ancestry relation changed
proposedSunnyReuse.characterMeaning: Here a character is a defined comparative linguistic feature, not simply a Unicode codepoint or an alphabet member.
minimumRecord: Observed, reconstructed and restored components separately
Proposed earlier and derived states plus direction-of-change evidence
proposedSunnyReuse.relationCriterion: Treat a grouping as a linguistic inheritance candidate only after a source-qualified derived feature, rather than mere resemblance/retention, is argued to characterize the compared members; assess its outgroup distribution and plausible alternatives. Missing observations remain unknown. A matching matrix does not prove the historical process.
proposedSunnyReuse.noWeights: Do not turn source repetition, feature count or Jev preference into a numerical historical authority score.
proposedSunnyReuse.finiteNextApplication: For one existing Secunda/Aramaic/Hebrew comparison, define a contextual feature and test the required direction, witnesses and contact alternatives. In the existing -αυεω case, the four edited surviving letters alone do not establish a shared innovation, an inheritance edge or a unique ancient phone.
proposedSunnyReuse.geometryBoundary: Only an independently specified adapter could carry these feature relations into SUNNY's musical/geometric representation. This method alone supplies no torus address, pitch ratio or biological genealogy.

negativeControls: An unchanged inherited feature does not isolate a daughter subgroup.
Shared new-looking forms can still arise through contact or independent development.
Unknown outgroup state is not evidence of absence.
Prestigious Tiberian-looking spelling in a Palestinian notation system need not identify a Tiberian spoken tradition.
A later manuscript's normalized Greek vowels do not alone demonstrate a change in living recitation.
Duplicated letters from PDF extraction are not linguistic innovations.
